text:
maria: FYI - BlueRiver Foods wants a 6-week on-prem POC in a food-processing facility. Requirements: fully air-gapped (no network egress at all), only physical media allowed (USB/air courier), hardware HSM is Thales Luna SA 7.5, strict FIPS requirement on crypto, SBOM and provenance required, and they mandate quarterly patch windows. They want: feasibility, offline activation flow, chain-of-custody for bundles, and a POC quote (Licensing + on-site eng days + courier). Can we scope?
sam: Re: HSM - Luna SA is PKCS#11-compatible which is good. But Thales often needs a vendor module and a dedicated management appliance. Clarify: do they want to bring their Luna instance and keys, or do they expect us to sign with our key and deliver?
maria: They will bring their Luna appliances and want the signing key to remain under their control. Also they wont allow installing kernel modules or extra daemons that require privileged kernel hooks.
leo: From runtime side: OK, userland PKCS#11 via our agent should work (we can load the Thales PKCS#11 module as an allowed library). No kernel modules needed. We need an operator workflow for offline signing and verification that runs on the appliance or an approved operator workstation inside the air-gapped perimeter.
tara: Security notes for questionnaire: we can provide signed SBOMs, reproducible build hashes, and bundle-level attestations. For FIPS: we have a FIPS build pipeline for TLS/crypto stacks; need to confirm if they need FIPS across the entire stack or just the signing/TLS operations. Also need to know whether they will require HSM-backed key unwrap for model artifacts.
sec-bot: Created ticket RDW-8341: "BlueRiver - sealed plant POC (Luna SA signing + offline activation)" assigned to @leo. https://redwood.example/tickets/RDW-8341
sam: Two feasible signing patterns: 1) Customer-sign (recommended): customer uses Luna to sign bundles with their private key. Our agent verifies signature before applying. 2) Redwood pre-sign + customer verification: we sign and provide chain-of-trust; customer validates using our public key. Pattern (1) meets their control requirement.
leo: Offline activation flow sketch:
- On our build farm we produce a signed bundle tarball + manifest.json (manifest lists version, commit, SBOM, checksums).
- We produce a detached signature request file that the operator imports to the Luna device to sign.
- Operator signs inside the air-gapped environment (via approved signing workstation) and returns signature file on USB.
- Installer verifies signature using PKCS#11 interface before install.
Example commands (concept):
```
# generate manifest locally
rdwctl bundle make --model quantized-rdw-7b --output rdw-bundle.tar.gz --manifest manifest.json
# create sig-request
rdwctl sig-request --manifest manifest.json > sigreq.bin
# operator signs with pkcs11-tool on Luna appliance (operator runs airgapped)
pkcs11-tool --module /opt/thales/lib/pkcs11.so -s -y privkey -i sigreq.bin -o sig.bin
# install verification
rdwctl verify --manifest manifest.json --sig sig.bin --pkcs11-module /opt/thales/lib/pkcs11.so
```
maria: They also want chain-of-custody notes for the courier (who signs receipt + timestamp) and optionally a tamper-evident seal id in the manifest. Add that to SOW.
tara: For patch cadence: we can ship quarterly cumulative bundles. For POC we can offer a one-off emergency hotfix path but it must be pre-approved and delivered via courier with operator acceptance. Hotfix SLA: offline acceptance required, expect manual apply time (aim <45m).
sam: Logistics & sizing: delta sizes depend on quantized weights + packaging. Typical incremental bundle 150MB-2GB; full model bundles can be 10-20GB if non-quantized. Recommend shipping compressed quantized artifacts for POC.
leo: Ops constraints: without any outbound egress we cannot phone-home license checks. Offline license model options:
- Time-limited activation token signed by customer HSM (preferred).
- Offline license file signed by Redwood + customer acknowledgement.
Both supported; token renewal must be handled via physical media.
maria: Pricing sketch: Private deployment license + on-site engineering days (2-5 days depending on integration), courier & handling per shipment, and optional FIPS validation support. Ben (finance) - can you provide standard POC on-site day rate and courier line items?
leo: I'll prep a sample signed manifest and an installer image that validates PKCS#11-signed bundles and post lab test notes to the ticket.
tara: I'll draft the SQ sections (SBOM, FIPS, telemetry disabled by default, audit logs written locally and exportable via signed archive). Please send me their questionnaire PDF.
maria: I'll schedule a 1hr presales + security + eng call with BlueRiver for Wednesday 9am PT. Also will ask them to confirm whether Luna admin appliance will be available to our engineer during the POC.
sec-bot: Added labels: "airgap", "luna", "fips", "poc-quote" to RDW-8341
sam: One more note - chain-of-custody: recommend we include a manifest entry: "seal_id" and a courier-sign block so they can tie physical package to manifest during verification.
maria: Great. Thanks everyone. I'll circulate the SOW draft and the scheduled invite. :white_check_mark:
